nodes.title: Cases
nodes.summary: A case and its hypotheses are written, validated and published as one thing.

nodes.title: Corporate Systems
nodes.summary: The systems of record every capability ultimately reads from, upstream of the normaliser.

nodes.title: Glossary
nodes.summary: The closed vocabularies and the registry of concepts that every other context speaks.

nodes.title: Integration
nodes.summary: The read-only capabilities that answer a concept, and the normalisation that keeps a corporate system's vocabulary out of the domain.

nodes.title: Investigation
nodes.summary: One run of a case against one subject — collect, judge each hypothesis, resolve the outcome the case declares, and record what happened.

nodes.title: Curated Knowledge
nodes.summary: The cases a specialist writes — which hypotheses a reported problem has, what confirms each one, and which one dominates which.

nodes.title: Action
nodes.summary: What the recipient of a referral does, drawn from a global vocabulary.

nodes.title: Concept
nodes.summary: A fact an investigation can collect, named once for the whole system and answered by exactly one capability.

nodes.title: Observation Field
nodes.summary: One named part of what the answer to a concept carries, and what a citation points at.

nodes.title: Outcome
nodes.summary: What an investigation concluded, contributed by each confirmable hypothesis and registered globally.

nodes.title: Recipient
nodes.summary: Who a referral goes to, named as an operational role.

nodes.title: Subject Type
nodes.summary: The kind of thing a case investigates, drawn from a closed vocabulary.

nodes.title: Capability
nodes.summary: What answers one concept — read-only, versioned, with a declared output schema and a deadline.

nodes.title: Assessment
nodes.summary: What the investigation concluded, what to do about it, which hypothesis decided it, and the text written for the recipient.

nodes.title: Citation
nodes.summary: The concept and the field an evaluation rested on.

nodes.title: Evaluation
nodes.summary: The verdict on one hypothesis, with what it rested on or why it could not decide.

nodes.title: Evidence
nodes.summary: What one capability answered about one concept, or the recorded fact that it did not answer.

nodes.title: Investigation
nodes.summary: One run of one case against one subject, written once and never changed.

nodes.title: Subject
nodes.summary: The one thing an investigation is about, named by its type and its identifier.

nodes.title: Case
nodes.summary: A published diagnostic procedure — its hypotheses in order of precedence, and what to do when none of them confirms.

nodes.title: Contract check unavailable
nodes.summary: What publication answers with when the capability registry cannot be consulted — that the check could not be decided, never that the case is wrong.

nodes.title: Case Under Edit
nodes.summary: The same case while a curator is still writing it, holding everything the case declares and not yet the version and hash publication assigns.

nodes.title: Hypothesis
nodes.summary: One falsifiable claim about what is wrong, with what must be collected to decide it and what follows if it holds.

nodes.title: Read failure
nodes.summary: What the reading of a case file answers with when its structured part does not parse — where the parse broke, and the text that says so to the curator.

nodes.title: Referral
nodes.summary: The action somebody takes and the role that takes it.

nodes.title: Refusal
nodes.summary: One reason one case did not pass validation — the rule that refused, the position in the case it refused at, and the text written for the curator.

nodes.title: Resolution
nodes.summary: What an investigation concluded and what somebody should do about it, taken together.

nodes.title: Capability query
nodes.summary: What the investigation context calls to have one concept answered about one subject.

nodes.title: Assessment reviewed
nodes.summary: An operator's judgement of an assessment, arriving later and from outside.

nodes.title: Investigation completed
nodes.summary: The fact that one investigation finished, carrying what it concluded and what it saw.

nodes.title: Case publication
nodes.summary: A case moves from being edited to being published, and publication is where its contract with the integration context is verified.

nodes.title: Diagnose
nodes.summary: One case run against one subject, from the attendant's choice to the written record and the response.

nodes.title: A lookup matches a published name exactly
nodes.summary: A term consulted in the glossary is compared to a published name character for character, the same comparison hypothesis names get.

nodes.title: A recipient is a role
nodes.summary: A referral goes to an operational role and never to a named person.

nodes.title: A capability is read-only
nodes.summary: The system diagnoses and refers, and never acts.

nodes.title: A registry lookup names a concept exactly
nodes.summary: The capability registry is consulted by the name of a concept, compared character for character, the comparison the whole published language already gets.

nodes.title: Evidence arrives in the glossary's vocabulary
nodes.summary: A corporate system's language stops at the normaliser.

nodes.title: One capability answers one concept
nodes.summary: The registry holds at most one capability for a concept, so nothing has to choose between two.

nodes.title: A decided evaluation cites evidence
nodes.summary: A verdict that confirms or refutes points at the concept and field it rested on, and the field must be one that concept declares.

nodes.title: An answer arrives within a declared deadline
nodes.summary: The attendant waits on the line, so the answer is produced within twenty seconds and inside the caller's timeout.

nodes.title: An inconclusive evaluation declares its reason
nodes.summary: An absent fact, a failed judgement and an exhausted deadline are three different things and never one.

nodes.title: An investigation is idempotent within a window
nodes.summary: The same question asked twice inside the window is one investigation, not two.

nodes.title: An investigation is written once
nodes.summary: No intermediate state of the domain ever persists.

nodes.title: An unattempted concept records a timeout
nodes.summary: A concept the collection never reached is an evidence carrying the timeout result, never an absent evidence.

nodes.title: Collection runs in the requester's scope
nodes.summary: What an investigation may see is bounded by what whoever asked for it may see.

nodes.title: A judgement never infers
nodes.summary: What the evidence does not give is inconclusive rather than filled in.

nodes.title: No stage aborts on its deadline
nodes.summary: Exhausting a deadline produces a recorded result and the investigation continues.

nodes.title: One evaluation per hypothesis
nodes.summary: Every hypothesis the case declares gets a verdict, and silence is not one.

nodes.title: One evidence per collected concept
nodes.summary: The evidence of an investigation is total over what its case collects — exactly one per concept, whatever happened to the attempt.

nodes.title: The outcome comes from the case
nodes.summary: Nothing produces an outcome or a referral except the case that declared them.

nodes.title: The response follows the record
nodes.summary: Nobody acts on an assessment that has no record, so the whole response waits for the write.

nodes.title: The writing input is narrowed
nodes.summary: A text cannot contradict the outcome if it never receives the material to.

nodes.title: A case does not publish without the contract check
nodes.summary: A capability registry that cannot be consulted is not permission to postpone the check to execution.

nodes.title: A case is one file
nodes.summary: A case is held by exactly one markdown file kept under version control, which is what lets a hash over that file identify the case whole.

nodes.title: A position indexes a hypothesis by name
nodes.summary: A refusal's position reaches a hypothesis by the name the curator gave it, and by its ordinal only where that name does not tell two of them apart.

nodes.title: A validation answers with every refusal
nodes.summary: A validation of a case runs every check it carries whatever an earlier one decided, and answers with all of them.

nodes.title: An unavailable check is not a refusal
nodes.summary: Where the registry cannot be consulted, publication says it could not decide, and never that the case is wrong.

nodes.title: An unreadable case is not validated
nodes.summary: A file whose structured part does not parse answers with a read failure, and no check of the validation runs over it.

nodes.title: A case has at least one hypothesis
nodes.summary: A case with no hypothesis investigates nothing.

nodes.title: Every term a case names exists in the glossary
nodes.summary: A case speaks only the published language, so nothing it names is invented in place.

nodes.title: A collected concept accepts the case's subject type
nodes.summary: A case cannot ask for a fact that does not apply to the kind of thing it investigates.

nodes.title: Every collected concept declares a ttl
nodes.summary: How stale a fact may be is stated by the concept, not assumed by whoever reads it.

nodes.title: Every collected concept has a read-only capability
nodes.summary: The contract between curated knowledge and integration is checked when publishing, not when running.

nodes.title: Hypotheses are ordered by precedence
nodes.summary: The order in which a case lists its hypotheses is the order in which their causes dominate one another.

nodes.title: A hypothesis collects at least one concept
nodes.summary: A hypothesis that collects nothing could never cite anything.

nodes.title: A hypothesis name is unique in its case
nodes.summary: Two hypotheses of the same case never share a name, because evaluations are indexed by it.

nodes.title: Nothing approves a publication
nodes.summary: Publishing a case is gated by the checks the case must pass and by nothing else — no person and no step approves it.

nodes.title: One falsifiable claim per criterion
nodes.summary: A criterion that holds for either of two reasons is two hypotheses.

nodes.title: Publication counts the version
nodes.summary: A published case's version is a sequential integer per slug that publication assigns, and it does the ordering the hash cannot.

nodes.title: The curator prose never changes what is collected
nodes.summary: Anything that changes what an investigation collects belongs in the structured part of the case.

nodes.title: The content hash covers the whole file
nodes.summary: A published case's hash is computed over the bytes of its whole file, the curator prose included, and never over a re-serialisation of what parsed.

nodes.title: The content hash is a named SHA-256
nodes.summary: A published case's hash is a SHA-256 digest written with the algorithm's name inside the value, so a later change of algorithm leaves no earlier pin ambiguous.

nodes.title: The contract check reads the current registration
nodes.summary: Publication asks the registry for the capability registered now for a concept, and never searches earlier versions of one.

nodes.title: The fallback follows what the collection returned
nodes.summary: When nothing confirms, the case answers with the no-data fallback where any evidence fell short, and with the exhausted fallback where every evidence answered.

nodes.title: The frontmatter holds everything the case declares
nodes.summary: The structured part of a case file is its frontmatter and the body below it is prose for the curator, and the frontmatter's delimiters are the boundary between them.

nodes.title: The text of a refusal comes from its rule
nodes.summary: The sentence a curator reads is declared by the rule that refused and carried by the refusal instantiated with the position.

nodes.title: The slug matches the file name
nodes.summary: A case's slug and the name of the file that holds it are the same name.

nodes.title: Two positions are two refusals
nodes.summary: The same rule refusing a case at two places produces one refusal per place, never one covering both.

nodes.title: What the curator reads is written in Portuguese
nodes.summary: Every text a validation or a publication addresses to the curator is written in the language the cases themselves are written in.
